section_path_text: Those Dirty Little Ships in the Mist
summary:
Those Dirty Little Ships in the Mist
All our professional lives we were taught that handymax tankers are built and make their profits in clean trading. Only those approaching the end of their useful lives trade dirty with worn out coatings whose replacement cost cannot be justified by the market. It was a sign that the grim breaker was nearing.

children.title: 2003 Average 4.9/Month
children.summary: A comparison of handymax spot fixture rates between the Black Sea and the Caribbean load areas shows that it is sometimes better to be in the Caribbean and sometimes not.

children.title: Black Sea
children.summary: Caribs The differential in WS points for handymaxes trading in the two load areas shows considerable variation over time. Whereas the differential in rates averaged 25 WS points over the entire period, it is obvious that the rate spread escalates greatly during the short days of winter when congestion becomes a significant problem in the Bosphorus.

children.title: WS Points
children.summary: Dirty trading in the Black Sea offers other inducements. Parcel sizes for Black Sea are 44,000 tons whereas parcel sizes in the Caribbean are about 37,000 tons.

children.title: Conclusion
children.summary: Perhaps we shouldn't disparage handymaxes giving up the joys of clean living for a little down and dirty trading. After all tankers are for making money, not for keeping up appearances.
